component.name: finbreak
component.summary: Understand your personal finances, privately and offline

description.p: finbreak is a private, offline desktop app for understanding your money. Import bank statements (CSV, OFX, or PDF), categorise transactions, and see where your money goes — with everything stored locally in an encrypted vault that only your password can open.

ul.li: Import statements from CSV, OFX, and PDF, with per-bank mappings
Automatic and rule-based transaction categorisation you can override
A spending dashboard with drill-down by category and merchant
Recurring-payment and transfer detection
Password-protected PDF reports and encrypted backups
Strong local encryption (SQLCipher AES-256, Argon2id key)
No accounts, no cloud, no tracking — your data never leaves your device

screenshot.caption: See where your money goes at a glance
Organise categories up to three levels deep
Spot recurring money — subscriptions, debit orders and salary
Transfers between your own accounts, kept out of spending
Auto-sort transactions with your own rules

ul.li: Imported credit-card statements no longer carry a stray "Continued on next page" on the last transaction of each page.
The README now explains how to name a desktop shortcut for the Linux AppImage, so you do not end up with two finbreak icons in the panel.
A remembered statement password no longer stays on an unrelated account when it moves to the correct one.
May statement dates no longer trigger a false "day and month might be swapped" warning.
A date format missing the year no longer files transactions in 1900 — the app now requires and checks for the year.
The import screen no longer re-reads the entire statement for every character you type in the date format box.
The import screen now has a Back button to return and adjust the column mapping if your import fails.
Unreadable amounts now show which value could not be read, instead of displaying internal error text.
Importing a damaged spreadsheet no longer closes the app when you change the Date column.
When no rows in an OFX or PDF statement can be imported, the error explanation now points to the per-row reasons instead of advising a column mapping screen.
The multi-file import table no longer hides unreadable rows when a statement has already been imported.
The Flatpak build now starts (it was missing a security library it did not actually use).
A statement with an unreadable line that moved money is now refused with an explanation, instead of importing with wrong totals.
The built-in install check now works on a computer with no display, such as a remote server.
Updated the library finbreak uses to verify that a downloaded update really came from us; the previous version had a published flaw (CVE-2026-69247).
Dependencies are now checked against two advisory databases rather than one, which catches a hijacked or typosquatted package that carries no CVE at all.
Release builds pin their build tools to exact, unchangeable versions, so nobody can silently repoint a tool at different code that would land inside a signed download.

Restoring a maliciously-crafted backup can no longer exhaust memory before you have logged in, a backup survives a power cut straight after saving, and one written into a shared folder cannot be hijacked.
Another user on the same computer can no longer stop finbreak from starting.
Import a whole folder of statements in one go — a mix of CSV, OFX and PDF — reviewing everything on one screen before anything is written.
Statements file themselves under the right account, read from the account number printed on them, and offer to create the account if it is new.
The dashboard says in a sentence what your month did, and stays quiet when the month is ordinary or the history is too short to judge.
Delete several statements at once, and confirm or reject several suggested transfers at once.
Importing a statement no longer re-sorts your whole history.
Accented shop names are matched consistently across import and categorisation.
Standard Bank statements now tell you when a line could not be read, instead of dropping it silently.
A Standard Bank statement with an out-of-range opening or closing balance is refused with a message instead of crashing the import.
An OFX file with an unusable closing balance is reported rather than failing silently.
Many smaller fixes across the Accounts, Forecast, Transactions and import screens.
The Accounts tab is now a sortable table of Name, Type, Account number, Note and Status, with columns you can resize and reorder.
Each account can store an account number and a free-text note, both held in the encrypted vault and masked on screen as dots plus the last four digits.
A "Show account numbers" tick-box reveals every account number in full for 30 seconds, then hides them again automatically.
The Forecast table and the Home dashboard breakdown lists now remember their column widths and order, like every other table in the app.
The dashboard scrolls instead of squashing when the window is too small, so the three breakdown columns stay readable.
Alerts moved off the dashboard into an "Alerts" button and dialog, so the page no longer shifts up and down as alerts come and go.
Only one copy of finbreak runs at a time — launching it again raises the window you already have.
Window → Reset layout now restores column widths and order as well as the window size, in the same click.
Running the AppImage no longer puts a duplicate finbreak icon in the taskbar.
The import preview table remembers your column widths between imports.
A new Forecast tab projects your balance forward from confirmed recurring income and expenses, to the end of the month or 30, 60 or 90 days ahead.
Spending alerts on the Home dashboard flag unusual spend, a newly-appeared recurring charge, or an expected debit that didn't post — each one dismissable.
Account-level balance reconciliation on the Accounts tab verifies that imported transactions bridge each statement's closing balance to the next.
The update prompt now lists what changed in every release you skipped, not just the newest one, and the download bar shows real progress.
The forecast no longer counts credit-card and loan debt as spendable cash; it anchors on current and savings accounts and names any account it excluded.
The Recurring and Transfers tabs show amounts with the currency symbol and thousands grouping, matching the rest of the app.
CSV import reports a friendly "not valid CSV" message instead of crashing on a corrupt or truncated file.
Updates install the exact bytes that passed the signature check, closing a window in which the payload could have been swapped on disk.
The auto-update check enforces HTTPS on redirects, not just the first request, so it cannot be silently downgraded to plaintext.
The password-hashing acceptance floor is separate from the vault-creation setting, so raising strength in future cannot lock existing vaults out.
Flatpak and native Linux packages (RPM + deb) — install finbreak via GNOME Software, KDE Discover, or your distro's package manager with a bundled, tested runtime.
Three-level category organization (Type › Category › Sub-category) with full rename, move and delete support at every level.
Report an Issue menu item; signed SHA256SUMS checksums and per-platform software-component lists (SBOMs) for independent release verification.
Password-safety features: vault reset for forgotten passwords and a Settings button to verify a backup is readable before restore.
Amounts display currency symbols correctly ("R 1,234.49") with a dedicated Currency column; confirmed transfers now show directionally on the Transactions tab.
Optional password hint on the unlock screen, stored unencrypted and readable before unlock as a memory aid (keep it vague, not your password).
Copy a transaction's amount or description with automatic clipboard clear after a configurable timeout (default 30 seconds) so sensitive data doesn't linger.
Unlock delays for repeated wrong password attempts — each retry gets slower (1s, then 2s, 4s, up to 30s) to defend against guessing attacks.
OFX import now files each transaction under the date the bank printed, even when the statement carries a timezone.
The delete-statement confirmation no longer over-states the loss when the statement overlaps another one you keep.
Deleting a statement no longer loses transactions that an overlapping statement still covers — they are handed over to the statement you keep.
